ov: The European wildcat: bigger and stouter than a house cat, with longer striped fur, a dark stripe along the back and a bushy, black-tipped tail. It lives mainly in broad-leaved and mixed forests, avoiding farmland and towns.

why.ac: Mainly nocturnal, but also out by day where people leave it alone.

len: Up to 65 cm, plus a 34.5 cm tail
wt: Males about 5–8 kg, females about 3.5 kg
rg: Continental Europe, Scotland, Turkey and the Caucasus. It has died out in England, Wales and Ireland.
df: Mainly small mammals such as rabbits and rodents, plus ground-dwelling birds.

cf.tip: The wildcat is bigger and stouter, with longer fur and a shorter, blunt, bushy tail.

fx: It interbreeds with domestic cats, which makes pure wildcats hard to tell from striped hybrids.
The northernmost wildcats live in northern and eastern Scotland.
